comments.author: intelliot
comments.body:
Suggested commit message:
```
`fixInnerObjTemplate`: set inner object template (#4906)

Add `STObject` constructor to explicitly set the inner object template.
This allows certain AMM transactions to apply in the same ledger:

There is no issue if the trading fee is greater than or equal to 0.01%.
If the trading fee is less than 0.01%, then:
- After AMM create, AMM transactions must wait for one ledger to close
  (3-5 seconds).
- After one ledger is validated, all AMM transactions succeed, as
  appropriate, except for AMMVote.
- The first AMMVote which votes for a 0 trading fee in a ledger will
  succeed. Subsequent AMMVote transactions which vote for a 0 trading
  fee will wait for the next ledger (3-5 seconds). This behavior repeats
  for each ledger.

This has no effect on the ultimate correctness of AMM. This amendment
will allow the transactions described above to succeed as expected, even
if the trading fee is 0 and the transactions are applied within one
ledger (block).
```

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Add an `STObject` constructor overload that includes an additional bool argument to set the inner object template. Set the argument to true if the constructed object is an inner object and if the `fixInnerObjTemplate` amendment is enabled.

### Context of Change

Currently, the inner object template is not set upon object creation. If the object contains an `soeDEFAULT` field, and this field is initially set to the default value, accessing the field results in `tefEXCEPTION` error. Conversely, if the top object's `soeDEFAULT` field, initially set to the default value, is accessed, it returns the default value since top objects have the template set during construction. This fix aims to make the inner object behavior consistent with the top object behavior. The inner object must be explicitly constructed, as described in the summary, for this fix to work.

Currently, two `AMM` fields, `sfTradingFee` and `sfDiscountedFee`, included in the inner objects `sfVoteEntry` and `sfAuctionSlot` respectively, are declared as `soeDEFAULT` fields. This fix employs the new `STObject` constructor when constructing inner objects that include these fields.

### Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Refactor (non-breaking change that only restructures code)
- [ ] Performance (increase or change in throughput and/or latency)
- [x] Tests (you added tests for code that already exists, or your new feature included in this PR)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Chore (no impact to binary, e.g. `.gitignore`, formatting, dropping support for older tooling)
- [ ] Release


## Test Plan

`AMM` unit-test is extended with a test, which demonstrates the behavior before and after this fix.

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body:
Our current setup for amendments works well when modifying and adding transactors. It works less well with bug fixes - especially bug fixes that effect lower level classes. We've run into this several times with STAmount and number classes, and now we're running into it with STObject. I dislike passing in a bool into the constructor like this patch does, although I understand why you did it.

What do you think about a `thread_local` variable that holds the current `Rules` (defaulting to a null ptr if there is no transaction active)? The variable would be setup on entry to a transaction and torn down on exit. The problems I see with this are:

1. It won't work with coroutines, since these can be resumed on different threads. I don't believe this is a problem now, but it could let bugs sneak in later if we use coroutines.
2. It wouldn't work with recursive transactions (which we don't have, but "batch" transactions may have a problem depending how they are implemented). This is fixable with a stack but could be another source of errors.
3. It may break leveling. This `thread_local` needs to sit at a lowest level of the hierarchy of a class that would use it. For now it could sit at the `protocol` level, which is fine. But later this could be an issue.

All in all I think I favor going in this directions, but thought I'd open it up for discussion. I'm leaving it as a comment on code because top-level comments cannot have threaded discussions.

reviewCommentsList.author: gregtatcam
reviewCommentsList.body:
I like this idea. This could be made into a more general solution then. The overloaded `STObject` constructor with `bool` argument is not needed and existing `STObject(SField const&)` constructor can be used instead. This variable can set/torn down in `applyTransaction()` and some added AMM code can be removed. This is somewhat similar to `thread_local Number::rounding_mode Number::mode_`. Does this sound right?

If `applyTransaction()` is the right place then wouldn't it address 2?

gregtatcam

reviewCommentsList.body: Yeah, it avoids those issues, but it may not be a better solution. Maybe you could just pass `Rules` (or more specifically `std::optional<Rules>` into the current ctor and not add the helper).

reviewCommentsList.body: I think this comment should copied to InnerObjectFormats.cpp, probably before line 138 (the closing `}`) or after line 27 (the opening `{`). That's where people are likely going to be making additions, and so will be more likely to see and heed the message.

reviewCommentsList.author: gregtatcam
reviewCommentsList.body: `auctionSlot` was originally fetched via `peekFieldObject()`, which was returning a reference to `auctionSlot`. The latest implementation constructs `auctionSlot` as the local variable, sets its fields, and then sets `auctionSlot` in `AMM` object. `set` originally had declaration only and was not implemented. I don't think it has to be gated.

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body:
The original code got an existing object and modified it. The new code creates a new object and sets it. So if there are any fields that aren't explicitly set that could have been present when it was retrieved in the previous version with `peekFieldObject` then those fields will be different between the old and new version and that's transaction breaking.

It looks like `sfAuthAccounts` is such a field. This looks transaction breaking without being protected with an amendment to me. If for some reason there's no way `sfAuthAccount` could have ever been set then we'd at the very minimum need a comment, but we'd probably want to rewrite this code to protect that case anyway.

As a side note, is it OK that `sfAuthAccounts` got overwritten with the new code or do we want to preserve that?

reviewCommentsList.author: gregtatcam
reviewCommentsList.body: `sfAuthAccounts` is an optional field and is not going to be present in either the old version or the new version. The final result in terms of which fields are present and which are not is the same in both versions. What changes is how `sfDiscountedFee` is handled when it's fetched from `sfAuctionSlot` because `sfDiscountedFee` is `soeDEFAULT`. The old version fails if the field is not present. The new version fails if the amendment is disabled and succeeds if the amendment is enabled.
